question: By what means does the departed spirit reach Yama's city, and what title identifies the third chapter?
premises: The departed spirit travels on the path through excellent cities in sequence
The departed spirit reaches the city of Yama by good and bad deeds
The text is located in the Bhṛṅgīśa Saṃhitā section on recollection of death truth
inference: The departed spirit proceeds sequentially to Yama's city according to deeds, and the third chapter is named the rite of worship for the departed and so forth.
uncertainties: mṛta+tatva+anusmaraṇe may be parsed as recollection of the truth of death or related senses (UNC)
pura+varāṇi could mean excellent cities or cities of boons; glossed in situ (UNC)
plain_english: On the path, that departed spirit goes in sequence through excellent cities to the city of Yama by good and bad deeds. Thus, in the venerable Bhṛṅgīśa Saṃhitā, in the recollection of the truth of death, the third chapter is named 'The Rite of Worship for the Departed and So Forth'.
